content.goal: Add a "dangerous" tool that must never run unsupervised.
content.why: For irreversible or expensive actions, the agent should PROPOSE, and a human should APPROVE. We add a tool worth gating. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 16, section 16.6.)
content.verify: The file saves. delete_file is registered and marked dangerous. It is exactly the kind of irreversible action that needs a human gate.

content.goal: Intercept dangerous tool calls and PAUSE for approval.
content.why: The pattern: the agent proposes an action; the system pauses and shows it to a human with context; the human approves, edits, or rejects. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 16, section 16.6.)
content.verify: When ATLAS requests delete_file, execution PAUSES and asks you to approve. Only on "y" does it proceed; on anything else it returns a rejection observation the agent can react to.
content.troubleshoot: If the pause never appears, confirm the loop calls run_tool_call_gated (not the un-gated dispatcher) for tool execution.

content.goal: Run a task that triggers the gate, and reject it.
content.why: A rejection must flow back as an observation so the agent adapts rather than crashing — human-in-the-loop is your backstop against mistakes AND injection. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 16, section 16.6.)
content.verify: ATLAS proposes deleting the file; you are prompted; if you answer "n", the deletion does NOT happen and ATLAS reports it could not complete that action. No irreversible action occurred without your approval.

content.goal: Place the gate at the FEW high-stakes points only.
content.why: Over-gating buries the user in prompts; under-gating is dangerous. Deciding WHERE the gates go is the real design work. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 16, section 16.6.)
content.code:
# Keep DANGEROUS_TOOLS small — only truly irreversible/expensive actions:
#   delete data, send money, email customers, change production.
# Safe, read-only tools (search_docs, get_word_count) must NOT be gated,
# or the tool becomes annoying and users abandon it.
content.verify: Only genuinely dangerous tools are in DANGEROUS_TOOLS. Read-only and harmless tools run without interruption; the gate appears only where the stakes are real.

content.goal: CHECKPOINT — high-stakes actions require a human.
content.why: This is the operational backstop against both ordinary model mistakes and successful prompt injection.
content.verify: All true — a dangerous tool exists; the agent proposes rather than executes it; a human approves/rejects, and rejection flows back as an observation; only the few high-stakes tools are gated. Next unit wraps ATLAS as a local API service with guardrails at the boundary.
